title: New skill: revalidate-done-tasks — periodic audit that done tasks are still actually done
description: A task's `state: "done"` records a snapshot of what was true when `pr-reviewer`/`pr-decision` last checked it — nothing currently re-checks that claim later. `orchestrate-tasks` only ever moves the board forward, so a later change elsewhere in the codebase (a deleted file, a renamed function, a quietly-removed test) could silently invalidate an earlier 'done' task's checklist claims without anything catching it. Create a new `.claude/skills/revalidate-done-tasks` skill that iterates every task under `docs/tasks/done/`, re-verifies each checklist item still holds against the current repository state (referenced files/functions still exist and do what the checklist claims), confirms the project's full test suites + coverage gates still pass overall (one full run is enough evidence for all done tasks, not a per-task re-run), and reports any task whose done-claim no longer holds — without silently fixing anything itself, matching the project's existing read-only-audit-agent pattern (e.g. `architecture-reviewer`, `elder-signal-reviewer`).

checklist.step: Design the audit's scope/mechanism — e.g. dispatching `task-qa-reviewer` once per done task vs. a single lighter-weight direct pass — and record the choice with rationale as a `decisions` entry, weighing thoroughness against the cost of potentially dispatching dozens of subagents on every run.
Create `.claude/skills/revalidate-done-tasks/SKILL.md` implementing the chosen approach, following existing skill file conventions.

Decide what the skill does with a task it finds no longer holds — most consistent with the project's existing rules is to flag it (revert `state` away from `done`, record a `decisions`/`questions` entry explaining why) rather than attempt an autonomous fix, matching the pipeline's existing philosophy of tracking findings on the board rather than an audit silently rewriting code — record as a `decisions` entry.
Register the new skill in CLAUDE.md's Skills list.
Run it once for real against the current (fully-done) board as a smoke test and report what it found (ideally nothing, confirming the board is currently accurate) before considering this done.

Fix the 'Handling a task that no longer holds' section (SKILL.md lines 36-45): it never says how to actually persist a flag given main's branch-protection ruleset rejects every direct push (CLAUDE.md). Every other task-board-writing agent in the project (task-worker: 'Never push directly to main', explicit branch/push/PR workflow) spells this out; this skill's steps 1-4 just git-mv and edit files with no commit/branch/PR mechanics, so following them literally on a main checkout leaves an unpersisted (or push-rejected) change. Add the missing branch/commit/push/PR steps, or otherwise state the intended persistence path explicitly.

Fix step 1 (SKILL.md line 18) / the test-suite step (line 26-30): neither instructs verifying the working tree is on an up-to-date `main` before enumerating done tasks, spot-checking file/function references, or running the test+coverage suites that are reported as 'shared evidence'. Given CLAUDE.md notes the shared working tree can be left on an arbitrary PR branch after a prior agent run, running this skill without first confirming/fetching latest `main` risks the audit's conclusions (clean pass, or a specific flagged task) being computed against the wrong code. Add an explicit 'fetch and check out latest main first' step.

decisions.decision: The skill's default mechanism is a single lightweight direct pass over all docs/tasks/done/*.json files — scripted existence checks for files/functions each checklist item names, plus one full run of the backend and frontend test+coverage suites shared as evidence for every done task — rather than dispatching task-qa-reviewer once per done task. A full task-qa-reviewer dispatch (its own test run, coverage run, and browser walkthrough per task) is reserved as an optional deeper dive the skill can suggest for one specific task the lightweight pass flags as suspicious, not run by default for all ~78 done tasks.
decisions.rationale: Dispatching task-qa-reviewer per done task was rejected as the default: at the board's current scale (~78 done tasks) that means ~78 full subagent runs — each with its own pytest/coverage/vitest invocation and, for UI-facing tasks, its own Playwright browser walkthrough — every time this skill runs. That cost makes the skill impractical to actually run periodically, which defeats its purpose (catching regressions in done work before they go unnoticed indefinitely). The lightweight pass still catches the specific failure mode this skill exists for (a referenced file/function silently disappearing, or a suite-wide regression) by running the real test suites once as shared evidence and spot-checking checklist claims directly against the repo, while keeping a full run tractable. This mirrors an existing pattern already used elsewhere in the project: check-coverage (cheap, broad status check) vs. test-90 (expensive, targeted fix pass), and architecture-reviewer/elder-signal-reviewer (targeted audits) vs. a full task-qa-reviewer re-verification.

decisions.decision: When the skill finds a done task whose checklist claim no longer holds, it never edits application code itself. It flags the task: git mv the task file back out of docs/tasks/done/ to docs/tasks/<id>.json, set state to "implementing" (clear code regression a task-worker can pick up) or "waiting_input" with a questions entry (genuine ambiguity, e.g. unclear whether the referenced behavior was deliberately removed elsewhere), append a decisions or questions entry describing exactly what broke with evidence, and mirror both state and path in docs/tasks/index.json in the same change.
decisions.rationale: Matches the project's existing read-only-audit-agent pattern (architecture-reviewer, elder-signal-reviewer, task-qa-reviewer all report/flag rather than fix) and the task-board philosophy of tracking findings on the board itself rather than a background process silently rewriting code no one asked it to touch. Rejected alternative: having the skill attempt an autonomous fix for simple cases (e.g. a renamed file) — rejected because even a 'simple' rename can hide a deliberate deeper change the skill has no way to distinguish from an accidental break, and CLAUDE.md's whole task-board model routes fixes through task-worker/PR/review, not a silent direct commit from an audit pass.

decisions.decision: The checklist's final smoke-test step was run as a full pass over all 78 docs/tasks/done/*.json files (not a sample): (1) index.json state/path mirror-consistency check across all 81 tasks — clean, no drift; (2) a scripted regex pass extracting every file-path-shaped and function-call-shaped string across all 78 done tasks' checklist text (114 path refs, 64 function refs) and checking each still exists/is defined in the repo — 4 apparent misses, all confirmed by manual follow-up to be false positives of the regex (two are checklist prose referencing another task's JSON file that has itself since moved into docs/tasks/done/, i.e. a stale literal path to a still-valid logical id-pointer per CLAUDE.md's own note on this; one is a checklist item verifying a value against docs/Analyse.md rather than an open 'decide X' judgment call, already explicitly reasoned through in that task's own review/pr_decision notes; one is an external SQLAlchemy library method (Session.get_bind()) mentioned in review prose, not an in-repo symbol; one is descriptive prose ('_wave_showed_state') paraphrasing behavior rather than naming a real function, and the actual underlying code path (evaluate_wave) was confirmed to still exist); (3) one full backend suite run (pytest --cov=app --cov-fail-under=90: 493 passed, 99.84% coverage) and one full frontend suite run (vitest run --coverage: 35 files/205 tests passed, 99.71% lines) as the shared regression evidence. No task was reopened — the board's ~78 done tasks currently hold up.
decisions.rationale: A full pass across the entire done-task set (rather than a sample) was feasible within this session because the checks are scripted/batched rather than per-task manual reads, exactly as the skill itself is designed to work — so this smoke test doubles as direct evidence the mechanism is efficient enough to actually run at full board scale, not just evidence the board is clean today.

comments.summary: BLOCKING: `.claude/skills/revalidate-done-tasks/SKILL.md`'s 'Handling a task that no longer holds' section (lines 36-45) git-mv's the task file and edits its JSON + index.json but never says how that change actually gets persisted, even though CLAUDE.md states main's branch-protection ruleset rejects every direct push, including a bookkeeping-only one. Every other task-board-writing agent (e.g. task-worker: 'Never push directly to main', with an explicit git fetch/branch/commit/push/PR workflow) spells this out explicitly; this skill's core 'flag it' step — its entire reason to exist, per its own description ('flags (never silently fixes)') — is not actually executable as written when run against main. Followed literally, it either leaves an uncommitted, easily-lost working-tree diff, or fails outright on push. Add the missing branch/commit/push/PR mechanics.

BLOCKING: neither step 1 (line 18, 'Enumerate every done task') nor the test-suite step (lines 26-30, run as 'shared evidence') instructs confirming the working tree is on an up-to-date `main` first. CLAUDE.md explicitly notes this shared working tree can be left on an arbitrary PR branch after a prior agent's run. Without an explicit fetch/checkout-latest-main step (which every other task-board agent, e.g. task-worker, states plainly), this skill's file/function existence checks and its test/coverage 'shared evidence' could be computed against a stale or unrelated branch — silently undermining the audit's whole purpose (either a false clean-pass on stale code, or missing a real regression that already landed on main).

Non-blocking: the 'Handling a task that no longer holds' section doesn't instruct getting a real current timestamp via `date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` before writing the `decisions`/`questions` entry a flag produces, unlike pr-reviewer's own instructions which explicitly call this out. Given this project's documented 'Orchestrator merge-ordering failure' memory note (a guessed/estimated timestamp breaking a downstream ordering check), this skill should carry the same explicit instruction. Tracked as docs/tasks/skill-revalidate-done-tasks-followups.json.

Non-blocking: the same section doesn't say what to do with a reopened task's pre-existing `review`/`pr_decision` fields, which still assert `verdict: "accepted"`/`"merge"` after the task is reverted to `implementing`/`waiting_input` — a future reader could be misled into thinking the task was re-confirmed accepted. Worth an explicit note. Tracked as docs/tasks/skill-revalidate-done-tasks-followups.json.

Non-blocking (code-review finding): the skill's own description invites 'periodic/scheduled' invocation, but neither the skill file nor CLAUDE.md's 'one agent at a time on the shared working tree' rule (which names task-worker/pr-reviewer/pr-decision/pr-merger explicitly) accounts for this skill potentially running while one of those is mid-flight on the same checkout — its git mv / index.json edits could intermix with an in-flight agent's uncommitted changes. Worth an explicit caveat in the skill (or an addition to CLAUDE.md's coordination rule once this skill is registered). Tracked as docs/tasks/skill-revalidate-done-tasks-followups.json.

Skill file is otherwise well-formed and matches existing conventions (architecture-review, check-coverage): frontmatter has name+description only (correct for a skill, not an agent), Steps/Output/Relationship-to-other-skills structure mirrors existing skills, and the description's trigger phrasing matches the project's style. Registered correctly in CLAUDE.md's Skills list.

The core audit mechanism (lightweight scripted spot-checks + one shared full test/coverage run, vs. a per-done-task task-qa-reviewer dispatch) is sound and its stated reasoning holds: a per-task dispatch would mean ~78 full subagent runs (each with its own pytest/coverage/vitest invocation, plus a Playwright walkthrough for UI-facing tasks) every time this skill runs, which is genuinely impractical for a periodic check. The chosen default mirrors the project's existing check-coverage-vs-test-90 and targeted-audit-vs-full-reverification patterns, as claimed. This part of the design is not in question — only the persistence/coordination gaps above.

Spot-checked the task-worker's claimed smoke-test run rather than trusting it at face value: reproduced the index.json state/path mirror check across all 81 tasks (0 mismatches, matches 'clean' claim); confirmed 78 done tasks exist under docs/tasks/done/ (matches the '~78' claim); independently scanned all done tasks' checklist+decisions text for backend/frontend source-path references (54 found, all resolve) and for docs/tasks/*.json path references (all 'misses' in my own broader scan were stale-but-valid literal paths to other tasks that have since moved into docs/tasks/done/, exactly the false-positive category described); directly confirmed the specific false positives claimed for the sampled tasks (get_analysis/analyse exist in backend/app/api/routers/stocks.py and backend/app/signals/engine.py; `_wave_showed_state` is genuinely absent from current code -- replaced by `_wave_lookback` in a later followups PR -- but only appears in decisions prose, never a checklist step, and the underlying evaluate_wave function it describes does still exist; Session.get_bind() is confirmed to be checklist prose about a real SQLAlchemy Session method used in a test file, not a claimed in-repo symbol). No unaddressed board regression found; the smoke-test's substantive conclusions hold even though the mechanism it validated has the persistence/staleness gaps noted above.

Re-ran both full suites myself on the checked-out PR branch and both match the task-worker's reported numbers exactly: backend `pytest --cov=app --cov-report=term-missing --cov-fail-under=90` -- 493 passed, 99.84% coverage (gate 90%); frontend `vitest run --coverage` -- 35 test files / 205 tests passed, 99.71% lines / 99.64% branches. No regression, gate comfortably met on both sides. No application code is touched by this PR (diff is .claude/skills/revalidate-done-tasks/SKILL.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/tasks/index.json, docs/tasks/skill-revalidate-done-tasks.json only) so this was a sanity check, not evidence of a change under test. No backend lint/type-checker is configured (confirmed via grep of backend/pyproject.toml), and frontend `eslint .` / `tsc -b` both ran clean.

No API route/schema touched (backend/openapi.json correctly untouched); no frontend component added/changed (step 7a n/a); no new module/dependency/layer added to the application itself, so a formal architecture-review pass doesn't apply here -- the project-philosophy-consistency check this review specifically asked for (the 'flag via reverting state + decisions/questions, never auto-fix' behavior) was checked directly against CLAUDE.md and confirmed consistent, independent of the persistence/staleness gaps above. This PR has no UI-facing surface (pure skill/doc/task-board change) -- browser walkthrough explicitly not applicable, not silently skipped. Decisions cross-check: all three original checklist items phrased as a judgment call have corresponding decisions entries with rationale and rejected alternatives.

review.notes: PR #92 needs work: two blocking gaps in the new SKILL.md's own documented mechanism (added to this task's checklist above), surfaced by the code-review skill and independently confirmed against the actual file content. (1) The 'Handling a task that no longer holds' section never specifies how a flag actually gets persisted given main's branch-protection ruleset -- every other task-board-writing agent in this project spells out the branch/commit/push/PR workflow explicitly, and this skill's core promise ('flags, never silently fixes') isn't actually executable as documented without it. (2) Neither the enumeration step nor the test-suite step instructs confirming the checkout is on up-to-date main first, which risks the audit's own evidence being computed against stale/wrong code -- directly undermining the tool's purpose. Both are squarely within what this review was asked to sanity-check ('its documented mechanism is actually sound/executable'). Everything else checked out clean: backend (493 passed, 99.84% coverage) and frontend (205 passed, 99.71% lines) suites both re-run clean on the checked-out branch, exactly matching the PR's claimed numbers (no application code is touched by this PR, so this was a sanity check rather than evidence of a change under test); no lint/type-check regression; the chosen lightweight-pass-vs-per-task-dispatch mechanism design itself is sound and its stated reasoning holds; the task-worker's claimed 78-task smoke test was independently spot-checked (index.json mirror, file/function reference scan, both full suite runs) and its substantive conclusions hold; the 'flag, never auto-fix' philosophy is consistent with the project's existing read-only-audit-agent pattern; no undocumented decisions; no UI surface, no API/schema change, no OpenAPI staleness. Three further non-blocking gaps (missing timestamp-capture instruction, no guidance on stale review/pr_decision fields on a reopened task, no shared-working-tree coordination caveat given the skill's own 'periodic/scheduled' framing) filed as docs/tasks/skill-revalidate-done-tasks-followups.json rather than blocking on their own. No pr_decision existed on this task prior to this review, so nothing to clear.
